decision: The ticket was closed at event-031 with final-check items unresolved: no landlord confirmation of completion on file (event-030 flagged "Need confirmation from landlord"), the provider invoice figure is unreconciled (GBP 75.11 with a 22 July 2026 due date at event-024 vs "£75 + VAT" reported at event-025), and event-022 shows the contractor still seeking to schedule a visit on 27/02, which conflicts with the completion report of 28/02. Within my mandate I recorded the inconsistencies (ACT-1) and asked the three owning parties for the facts that settle them: contractor for attendance date, work done and invoice total (RTE-CONTRACTOR); landlord for confirmation that the job is complete at that cost (RTE-LANDLORD); tenant for confirmation the machine now heats on 60°C+ (RTE-TENANT). No new dispatch, no spend and no payment were made; liability was not decided. The repair itself (appliance wiring to the heating element) carries no reported hazard — no burning smell, sparks or shock risk in any artefact, and the property's own hot water was unaffected (event-002) — so no emergency switch and no safety red flag, only the recorded check.
recap: Closed washing-machine repair reopened at final checks: invoice amount, attendance date and landlord confirmation unreconciled; asked contractor, landlord and tenant.
hold_reason: Waiting for Provider — Lantern Services to confirm attendance date, work done and invoice total (3 working days, from ACT-2); then Waiting for Landlord for confirmation of completion (ACT-3).
next_step: Lantern Services to confirm attendance date, work carried out and the final invoice total incl. VAT within 3 working days; then landlord (Mercer) to confirm completion at that cost before the ticket can stand as closed.
